title: ALBERT shared layers + depth Mirror
hypothesis: A small depth-specific Givens view on a fully tied repeated block recovers layer-role differentiation on held-out digits more effectively than hard sharing and equal-code FiLM, while retaining less than 60% of untied payload.
physical_object: One 64-dimensional residual block applied at three logical depths; block contains separate attention-like linear residual map A and FFN-like two-layer residual map F.
mirror_coordinate: Four Givens angles per depth on first eight channels after each repeated block; shared physical A/F remain tied.
logical_multiplicity: Three logical depth roles backed by one tied physical block.

methods: untied A and F per depth
A tied only, F private by depth
F tied only, A private by depth

development.selection: mean validation NLL across all methods
development.allowed_tuning: select base learning rate only from frozen grid

success_gate: On all fresh worlds, tied+Mirror improves accuracy over fully tied by >=1pp, stays within 2pp of untied, uses <=60% untied bytes, and beats equal-byte FiLM by >=1pp or saves >=10% bytes at <=0.5pp loss.
failure_gate: Fails tied/untied quality-storage gate in >=2 fresh worlds or simpler FiLM matches/dominates at equal/lower payload and compute.
boundaries: small digits residual-block proxy, not ALBERT/BERT reproduction
no capacity claim from fixed update count
